transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Emma Lawson (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (FinOptima - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Nadia Riaz (Security), Marcus Lee (SRE)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick weekly sync for POC onboarding progress; focus on access/setup for VPC peering and service accounts, remaining infra blockers, schedule for benchmarking, and security review items (KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs). Agreed to a benchmark run next week and to share network diagram and SOC2 artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah it's the weekly POC check-in for FinOptima, I'll quickly run through agenda, then Diego will cover the infra checklist and then we'll go over security questions, scheduling the benchmark, etc.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks Emma, quick note - we've been training some evals locally and are keen to see inference latencies on our own traffic, so the benchmark next week is high priority.
[00:30] Diego: Cool, I'll cover the benchmark plan, and also current access - Marcus, can you confirm service account access? last week I think you were setting up the role for the dedicated cluster.
[00:44] Marcus: Yep, I created the service account, we've granted the minimal IAM roles but we still need the VPC peering details from your side, Emma. The peering request shows pending.
[00:58] Emma: Right, I sent the network diagram in the shared drive earlier, but I'll re-send the updated POC network diagram with explicit CIDR ranges and firewall rules after this call.
[01:12] Liam: One thing from platform side - we need the external egress ip ranges for the hosted endpoint for allowlisting, and also want to understand if dedicated requires egress through our NAT or if Redwood manages outbound connectivity.
[01:30] Diego: For dedicated, egress depends on your deployment choice; with the VPC attachment option traffic can egress via your VPC/NAT, otherwise if you use Redwood-hosted we have controlled egress ranges. We'll send a config doc to show both options.
[01:45] Nadia: On the security front, can you confirm if key management uses customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys, and do audit logs include per-request details?
[02:00] Emma: Good question. Diego, can you cover KMS and audit logs?
[02:05] Diego: Sure - we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via supported KMS providers. Audit logs will capture request metadata and model version info; token-level logs are optional and we can redact payloads for compliance. Note: in the docs sometimes the term KV cache shows up weirdly in the export but the logs include model route and latency.
[02:26] Priya: That's helpful. For compliance, Nadia will need SOC 2 and the encryption matrix.
[02:33] Nadia: Yes please, and we need SSO/SAML integration details - SAML metadata, IdP support, and RBAC roles.
[02:42] Emma: We'll share the SOC2 package and SAML integration guide. Diego, can you put together a one-pager?
[02:48] Diego: Yep, I'll upload the docs to the shared folder.
[03:00] Emma: Ok quick status round for onboarding items: 1) VPC peering pending from Redwood (Emma to re-send) - Marcus to confirm once peered; 2) Service account created, keys pending rotation settings; 3) Benchmark schedule - proposed Fri 22nd 09:00 PT; 4) Security docs to be shared.
[03:18] Marcus: I'll verify peering and also confirm firewall ports for the health endpoints, we had a mismatch earlier (443 vs 8443) in the sample config.
[03:32] Diego: Note on the firewall - Redwood's sidecar expects inbound from your subnet to the cluster on 443. The 8443 note is from an old on-prem example, sorry for the confusion.
[03:47] Priya: On the ML side, our eval includes variable sequence lengths and batching; Diego, do you have guidance for model selection (quantized vs full fp16) and how that will affect latency/cost?
[04:02] Diego: Yes - for inference throughput and cost we'd recommend starting with a quantized variant (8-bit/4-bit) for the initial benchmark; provides big cost benefits. However, for accuracy sensitive tests, run a small sample with fp16 as well to compare quality. We'll include config flags and expected perf deltas in the doc.
[04:24] Priya: Great. Also, can we use your streaming responses for our UI? There's some jitter in our frontend with chunking.
[04:34] Emma: Streaming is supported - Diego, note to provide sample client code with streaming and reconnection behavior.
[04:41] Diego: Will do. Also, small note - when we run benchmarks we want to simulate KV cache warm/cold starts; we'll provide modes in the runner.
[04:55] Liam: About routing - we might need to route low-latency traffic to a smaller model and batch background requests to a cheaper model; does Redwood support automatic fallback?
[05:08] Diego: Yes, smart routing / fallback policies are supported; you can pin routes to model variants and set canary rules. We'll share an example routing policy. There's also auto-batching that you can tune for latency vs cost.
[05:24] Nadia: For the SOC review, is there an isolated audit log for PII redaction, and do you support field-level redaction?
[05:35] Diego: We support payload redaction at ingestion and can configure field-level scrubbing in the pipeline; we'll note limitations in the doc.
[05:44] Emma: Quick callout - the customer's data residency requirement: Priya, you mentioned EU-only storage?
[05:51] Priya: Yes for some datasets we need EU-only storage; we want to confirm Redwood Private options or hosted EU regions.
[05:59] Emma: Redwood Private or Dedicated in EU region can satisfy that. Diego, can you give a short note on deployment options?
[06:08] Diego: Sure - Hosted API is fastest to get started but may not meet strict residency; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a region; Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives full control. We'll include the tradeoffs table in the doc.
[06:23] Marcus: From SRE side, we also need metrics and tracing hooks. Are there per-route dashboards?
[06:30] Diego: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks for spans. Some sensitive metrics can be redacted.
[06:41] Priya: Ok, anything blocking the benchmark besides VPC peering and keys?
[06:47] Emma: I think that's it, and schedule alignment.
[06:51] Priya: One more question - pricing during the POC, are we on a trial credit or billed usage?
[07:00] Emma: You're on the POC credits provided to evaluate; we'll send a short pricing note comparing hosted vs dedicated per-token estimates for your traffic pattern.
[07:12] Liam: Great, please include cost estimates for both the quantized and fp16 runs.
[07:18] Diego: We'll produce a small spreadsheet with expected tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and latency estimates.
[07:28] Emma: Alright let's go into the infra checklist that Diego prepared - Diego?
[07:33] Diego: Infra checklist: 1) VPC peering + CIDR confirmed; 2) Service account + IAM roles; 3) NAT / egress allowlist; 4) Firewall port 443; 5) KMS access if customer-managed; 6) SAML SSO metadata exchange; 7) Benchmark runner access keys. Status: item 1 pending, item 2 done, item 3 in progress, item 4 pending confirmation, item 5 pending if they choose customer KMS, item 6 pending (we need IdP metadata), item 7 will be created once peering is confirmed.
[08:08] Marcus: For item 4, I'll confirm ports after peering. For item 6, Nadia will share IdP metadata by end of day.
[08:16] Nadia: I'll share SAML metadata to the shared folder. One question - do you support Just-In-Time provisioning or SCIM?
[08:25] Diego: SCIM is supported for user provisioning. We'll include endpoints and sample payloads.
[08:33] Priya: On the benchmark, please include a cold-start test and a warmed-KV-cache test so we can see differences.
[08:42] Diego: Absolutely. We'll run both.
[08:47] Emma: Let's lock the benchmark window - proposed 2026-05-22 09:00 PT. Marcus, can you commit to having peering tested by then?
[08:56] Marcus: I'll prioritize it, but if there's delay, can we move to a backup slot Monday 25th?
[09:02] Emma: Yes we'll plan a backup.
[09:05] Priya: Also please ensure any PII in logs is redacted before we send samples to your team.
[09:12] Diego: We'll configure scrubbing and also provide an isolated access path for logs.
[09:18] Emma: Ok small list of action items coming out of this call - I'll read them out.
[09:23] Emma: Action items: 1) Emma to re-send updated POC network diagram and include CIDRs + firewall rules (due 2026-05-21). 2) Diego to upload SOC2 + KMS docs and SAML/SCIM integration guide to shared folder (due 2026-05-22). 3) Diego to prepare benchmark runner configs and spreadsheet for cost/latency (due 2026-05-21). 4) Marcus to confirm VPC peering and firewall ports (due 2026-05-21). 5) Nadia to share IdP metadata and compliance requirements (due 2026-05-21).
[09:48] Priya: Sounds good. One last minor note - there's a previous note in the worksheet referencing 'KV cache' abbreviation that our auditors flagged as unclear; can you expand that in docs?
[09:58] Diego: Yep will add a short explainer on KV cache semantics and warm/cold impacts.
[10:04] Emma: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and confirm the benchmark time.
[10:10] Priya: Thanks, appreciate it.
[10:12] Emma: End call.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Emma to re-send network diagram + CIDR + firewall rules (2026-05-21).
- Diego to share SOC2, KMS details, SAML/SCIM docs, and benchmark configs (2026-05-22).
- Schedule benchmark for 2026-05-22 09:00 PT (backup 2026-05-25).
- Marcus to confirm peering and firewall ports (2026-05-21).
